body.statement:
Fix \((P,B^0,\varepsilon,\pi_0)\in\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\), and let \(\mathcal O_G\) be its observed moments for an arbitrary view graph \(G\).  Then
\[
 \Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V,
 \qquad
 \Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}.
\]
More precisely, for every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\) there is a centered jointly Gaussian witness in \(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\) with coefficient family \(B_\pi\) and the same observed covariance blocks.  Its within-view disturbance coordinates are independent and nondegenerate, while its off-diagonal cross-view residual covariances are retained as unrestricted nuisance covariances rather than tested for zero.
body.proof_tex:
Stack the views in a fixed order, write
\(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}=\operatorname{Cov}_P((X^{(a)})_{a\in M})\), and
fix \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\).  The argument in
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), applied within every view, shows
that \(\Sigma^{aa}\succ0\); hence all regressions defining
\(B_\pi^{(a)}\) exist.  Put
\[
 \mathcal L_\pi=\operatorname{diag}_{a\in M}(L_\pi^{(a)}),
 \qquad
 S_\pi=\mathcal L_\pi\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\mathcal L_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Each \(L_\pi^{(a)}\) is unit lower triangular after reindexing by \(\pi\),
so it is invertible.  Since \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}\) is a covariance
matrix, (2) gives \(S_\pi\succeq0\).

We next identify its within-view blocks.  Let
\(e_k^{(a)}\) be the residual from regressing
\(X_{\pi(k)}^{(a)}\) on
\((X_{\pi(1)}^{(a)},\ldots,X_{\pi(k-1)}^{(a)})\).  The normal equations
give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)})=0
 \quad(\ell<k).
 \tag{3}
\]
For \(\ell<k\), the earlier residual \(e_\ell^{(a)}\) is a linear
combination of \(X_{\pi(1)}^{(a)},\ldots,X_{\pi(\ell)}^{(a)}\), all of
which lie in the predecessor span in (3).  Therefore
\(\operatorname{Cov}_P(e_k^{(a)},e_\ell^{(a)})=0\).  Moreover, positive
definiteness of \(\Sigma^{aa}\) implies that the residual variance is the
strictly positive Schur complement
\[
 d_{k,a}=\Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),\pi(k)]-
 \Sigma^{aa}[\pi(k),A_{k-1}]
 \{\Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},A_{k-1}]\}^{-1}
 \Sigma^{aa}[A_{k-1},\pi(k)]>0.
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus every diagonal block \(S_\pi^{aa}=R_\pi^{aa}\) is diagonal with a
strictly positive diagonal.

Choose an orthogonal diagonalization
\(S_\pi=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{mp})U^{\mathsf T}\),
where \(\lambda_s\ge0\), and set
\(S_\pi^{1/2}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\lambda_1},\ldots,
\sqrt{\lambda_{mp}})U^{\mathsf T}\).  If \(g\) has \(mp\) independent
standard normal coordinates, define
\[
 \widetilde\varepsilon=S_\pi^{1/2}g,
 \qquad
 \widetilde X=\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}\widetilde\varepsilon.
 \tag{5}
\]
Then \(\widetilde\varepsilon\) is centered jointly Gaussian with covariance
\(S_\pi\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde X)
 =\mathcal L_\pi^{-1}S_\pi\mathcal L_\pi^{-\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_{\mathrm{full}}.
 \tag{6}
\]
For a fixed view \(a\), its disturbance covariance is the positive diagonal
matrix in (3)--(4).  Its characteristic function therefore factors as
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(i\sum_{j\in V}t_j
 \widetilde\varepsilon_j^{(a)}\right)
 =\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12\sum_{j\in V}d_{j,a}t_j^2\right)
 =\prod_{j\in V}\exp(-d_{j,a}t_j^2/2),
\]
which proves that the within-view coordinates are independent, centered,
and nondegenerate.  Equation (5) also gives
\(\widetilde X^{(a)}=B_\pi^{(a)}\widetilde X^{(a)}+
\widetilde\varepsilon^{(a)}\), and the coefficient matrices share the order
\(\pi\).  Thus the witness belongs to
\(\mathfrak M_{p,m}^{\mathrm{pub}}\).  By (6), it matches every observed
diagonal block and edge block, so the existential definition in
\(\texttt{def:compatible-orders}\) gives
\(\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\).

Since \(\pi\) was arbitrary and the reverse inclusion
\(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\subseteq\mathfrak S_V\) is part of the definition,
\(\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)=\mathfrak S_V\).  The formula for
\(\Theta_G\) follows from \(\texttt{def:identified-tuple-set}\).  Finally,
the cross-view blocks of \(S_\pi\) in (2), including their off-diagonal
coordinate entries, were carried into the Gaussian witness without any zero
constraint.  They are therefore nuisance covariance, not an observable
root-screening condition in the published class.
body.justification: The theorem gives the explicit Gaussian witness certifying the exact unrestricted-cross-view boundary and prevents invalid q-screening in the published class.
body.gap: The anchor's structural model allows cross-view nuisance dependence, but no supplied result identifies the complete second-moment compatible-order set under that unrestricted dependence.
body.consumer: Analysts learn that partial cross-view covariance cannot prune marginal orderwise coefficient tuples without an additional cross-view restriction.
